P01.rationale: A large portrait of the client (David Cordes) occupies roughly the top half of the left column, making it a prominent human anchor, though it shares space with overlaid text elements.

P05.rationale: The client portrait is clearly framed and named ('Cordes Consulting / David Cordes') at meaningful size occupying approximately a third of the left column.

P07.rationale: A single pull-quote testimonial from the named CEO is present but there is no press/logo wall, rating cards, or review grid — social proof is minimal.

P10.rationale: Oversized decorative numerals ('3' and '2') are overlaid on the portrait image as large ghost/decorative typographic elements, plus large standalone stat numerals on the right column.

P11.rationale: A partial donut/arc chart tied to the '50%' efficiency figure is present alongside discrete numeric stats (6 processes, 0 migrations), providing data-bound visualisation.

P12.rationale: The layout is reasonably dense with a large portrait, structured body copy sections, stat block, and testimonial, though the right column has some breathing room that keeps it from fully magazine-dense.

P13.rationale: The background is a plain off-white/cream with no intentional texture or atmospheric treatment beyond the flat colour.

P14.rationale: The portrait photo has a subtle darkening/desaturation treatment that allows the overlaid white 'Monate' text and numerals to remain legible.

P16.rationale: No device or product mockup (phone, laptop, book) appears anywhere on the page.

N07.rationale: The portrait appears to be a specific, named individual in a professional setting rather than obvious stock imagery, lending reasonable specificity.

N08.rationale: There is some open whitespace in the right column between the stat blocks and testimonial, but it is not excessive or purposeless — it aids readability.

N10.rationale: Text ('Monate' and the large '3') sits directly on the portrait photo but the image is sufficiently dark/blurred in that region to maintain adequate legibility.
